forces: Release Please converts deliberate Refs footers into closing directives that GitHub executes when a release PR merges into the default branch, changing authoritative tracker state.
Issue links and all other suffix bytes must survive neutralization, while distinct non-merge identical subjects and intermediate commits remain preserved.
Checks must inspect raw selected input independently of cleaning and name any remaining closing directive, including keyword-only changes with zero duplicate removals.
The allowed implementation boundary is the cleaner and its existing tests, not Release Please configuration, manifest or workflow, and introduces no dependency or credential changes.
The canonical suffix-preservation clause must be replaced by a capability delta under a full governance-core assessment before implementation.

security_justification.audit_integrity: This is release-note and tracker integrity, not runtime audit-event integrity. Preserve commit and issue links while removing the false claim of closure; the frozen audit contract and SDK event pipeline are unchanged.
security_justification.authentication_or_authorization: Reuse existing GitHub REST token handling and permissions. No authentication mechanism, permission scope, secret, production authorization or SDK authority gate is added or modified.
security_justification.authority_provenance: Keep original commit hashes and issue URLs as release provenance. GitHub Issues remains the authoritative execution tracker; a reference-only release must not stand in for an issue completion decision.
security_justification.concurrency: No shared-state or concurrency primitive changes. Existing release automation may regenerate text, but deterministic cleanup and the existing edited-description check are reused without adding races or workflow orchestration.
security_justification.confidentiality: The rewrite operates on public release markdown and git metadata, not confidential events. No token, header or response logging is added; existing REST credential handling remains unchanged.
security_justification.cryptography: No cryptographic algorithm, key, signature, hash protocol or verification claim changes. Commit identifiers are retained as provenance links, not introduced as a new security mechanism.
security_justification.error_disclosure: New check diagnostics name public offending release entries or lines so an owner can repair them. They require no environment, token or request-header disclosure and introduce no runtime audit error channel.
security_justification.external_security_integration: The cleaner continues to use only the existing GitHub REST description endpoint with built-in fetch. No SIEM, production transport, third-party action or external security service is introduced.
security_justification.fail_posture: Raw selected inputs are checked independently of cleaned output; a closing directive fails and names its line. Existing malformed-entry, unresolved-commit and REST failures stay fatal; checks never rewrite dirty input.
security_justification.lifecycle: The change concerns release-PR notes before merge, not SDK or audit-operation lifecycle. Unchanged version ranges continue to skip; v0.22.0 history and later separate fold/archive tickets are not mutated here.
security_justification.mutation_ownership: Source edits are bounded to cleaner and tests under the active packet. During normal cleanup only selected release text and its PR description change; no direct tracker writes, version moves or config/workflow edits are added.
security_justification.privacy_transformation: This is a closing-keyword transformation of public release markdown, not personal-data processing, redaction or telemetry collection. Issue URLs and other suffix bytes stay intact without new data collection.
security_justification.resource_retention: No persistence layer, queue, retention policy or background process is introduced. Planted-control tests use external disposable fixtures removed in finally blocks rather than retaining mutated live source.
security_justification.retry_or_redelivery: Repeated cleaning of refs is idempotent and an unchanged body is not PATCHed. Existing REST failure behavior remains fatal; no retry, delivery primitive, outbox or audit-event redelivery behavior is changed.
security_justification.trust_boundary: Markdown remains data consumed by the existing cleaner and check, never shell instructions. Preventing GitHub's closing interpretation does not move a runtime security boundary or add a new credential-bearing integration.
